prompt: Show that $y=Ce^{2x}-\tfrac12$ satisfies $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2y+1$ for any constant $C$.
markscheme: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=2Ce^{2x}$ **(A1)**; $2y+1=2Ce^{2x}-1+1=2Ce^{2x}$ ✓ **(A1)** — a general solution contains an arbitrary constant fixed by an initial condition.

prompt:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=x+y$, $y(0)=1$.

**(a)** Use Euler's method with step $h=0.1$ to estimate $y(0.2)$. **[2]**

**(b)** The exact solution is $y=2e^{x}-x-1$. Find the percentage error and explain why Euler's method underestimates here. **[2]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $y_1=1+0.1(0+1)=1.1$; $y_2=1.1+0.1(0.1+1.1)=1.22$ **(M1)(A1)**

**(b)** Exact $y(0.2)=1.2428$; error $\approx1.8\%$ **(A1)**. The solution curve is concave up, so each tangent step lies below the curve **(R1)**

prompt:
A cup of tea cools according to $\dfrac{dT}{dt}=-k(T-20)$, where $T$ °C is its temperature after $t$ minutes. $T(0)=90$ and $T(10)=60$.

**(a)** Solve the differential equation to show that $T=20+70e^{-kt}$. **[3]**

**(b)** Find $k$, and the time for the tea to cool to 30 °C. **[3]**
markscheme:
**(a)** $\displaystyle\int\frac{dT}{T-20}=-\int k\,dt\Rightarrow\ln|T-20|=-kt+c$ **(M1)(A1)**; $T-20=Ae^{-kt}$ and $T(0)=90\Rightarrow A=70$ **(A1)**

**(b)** $40=70e^{-10k}\Rightarrow k=\dfrac{\ln(7/4)}{10}\approx0.0560$ **(A1)**; $10=70e^{-kt}\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{\ln7}{k}\approx34.8$ min **(M1)(A1)**

prompt: Use the substitution $y=vx$ to solve $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{x^{2}+y^{2}}{xy}$, $x>0$, given $y=2$ when $x=1$.
markscheme:
$\dfrac{dy}{dx}=v+x\dfrac{dv}{dx}$ and RHS $=\dfrac1v+v$ **(M1)(A1)**

$x\dfrac{dv}{dx}=\dfrac1v\Rightarrow\displaystyle\int v\,dv=\int\frac{dx}{x}$ **(M1)**, $\dfrac{v^{2}}{2}=\ln x+c$ **(A1)**

$x=1$, $v=2$: $c=2$ **(A1)**; $y^{2}=x^{2}(2\ln x+4)$, i.e. $y=x\sqrt{2\ln x+4}$ **(A1)**
